title: SDDC Manager host inventory sweep over a page-repeating collection
prompt:
The `vcfhosts` Go module in this workspace is meant to export the ESXi host inventory of a VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 SDDC Manager, but only the fixture, the protected checks and the README exist so far. Build the rest.

The inventory comes back a page at a time, and SDDC Manager pages it without a stable ordering on the server side, so the same host can be handed back on two consecutive pages. The export has to cover every page, count each host once, and emit what it collected in an order that does not depend on how the pages happened to fall.

Do not modify `verification/`, `scripts/verify.sh` or `testdata/hosts.json`. Use the standard library only: the checks run with the module proxy switched off, so a third-party dependency will not resolve.

## 1. Pin the contract in `docs/contract.json`

Derive it from the SDDC Manager OpenAPI document VMware publishes:

* repository `vmware/vcf-api-specs`
* file `specifications/sddc-manager/sddc-manager-openapi.json`
* at tag `9.0.0.0` — not `main`, and not the 9.1 revision of the same file

Fetch that document and read the values out of it. Do not work from an HTML API reference page or from memory; the values below come from the specification document itself. The contract names two operations and nothing else: `createToken` and `getHosts`.

`docs/contract.json` is decoded strictly — a field name outside this shape is an error, so use exactly these names:

```json
{
  "spec": {
    "repository": "<owner/repo>",
    "path": "<the document's path inside that repository>",
    "tag": "<the tag>",
    "commit": "<the 40-character commit sha that tag points at, lower case>",
    "openapi": "<the document's top-level openapi field>",
    "title": "<the document's info.title>",
    "version": "<the document's info.version>"
  },
  "operations": [
    {
      "operationId": "<...>",
      "method": "<HTTP method, upper case>",
      "path": "<the path as written in the document, including its version prefix>",
      "summary": "<the operation's summary>",
      "successStatus": 200,
      "responseSchema": "<component schema name of that response's application/json body>",
      "errorStatuses": [400, 500],
      "requestBody": {
        "required": true,
        "contentType": "<the media type>",
        "schema": "<component schema name of the body>",
        "properties": ["<the body schema's property names, in document order>"]
      },
      "queryParameters": [
        { "name": "<...>", "type": "<the parameter schema's type>", "required": false }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "pagination": {
    "operationId": "<the operation that pages>",
    "pageParameter": "<...>",
    "sizeParameter": "<...>",
    "elementsField": "<...>",
    "metadataField": "<...>",
    "pageNumberField": "<...>",
    "pageSizeField": "<...>",
    "totalElementsField": "<...>",
    "totalPagesField": "<...>"
  }
}
```

Rules for filling it in:

* `successStatus` is the operation's single 2xx response code, as a number. `errorStatuses` are the remaining response codes the document declares for it, ascending.
* `summary` is the operation's summary exactly as the document writes it.
* `requestBody` is omitted entirely for an operation that takes no body. `properties` lists the body schema's property names in document order.
* `queryParameters` is omitted entirely for an operation that takes none, and otherwise lists every query parameter of that operation in document order, each with the type its schema gives it.
* `pagination` describes the operation that pages: `pageParameter` and `sizeParameter` are the two query parameters *this tag* gives it for paging, and both must appear in its `queryParameters`. A later VCF revision of the same file added differently named paging parameters — take the names this tag declares. `elementsField` and `metadataField` are the properties of that operation's response schema; `pageNumberField`, `pageSizeField`, `totalElementsField` and `totalPagesField` are the properties of the metadata schema it refers to.

## 2. Record the source in `docs/official_sources.json`

```json
{
  "sources": [
    {
      "title": "<what the document is>",
      "url": "<https link into the repository>",
      "repository": "<owner/repo>",
      "license": "<the repository's SPDX license identifier>",
      "path": "<the document's path>",
      "tag": "<the tag>",
      "commit": "<the commit sha>",
      "operationIds": ["<the operations the contract names>"]
    }
  ]
}
```

Exactly one entry. `url` must pin the commit sha rather than a branch or a tag, and must end with the document's path. `repository`, `path`, `tag` and `commit` must agree with `spec` in `docs/contract.json`.

## 3. `pkg/mock` — a loopback SDDC Manager pinned to that contract

```go
package mock

type Config struct {
    ContractPath string // docs/contract.json, the contract the server is pinned to
    FixturePath  string // the JSON array of hosts the server pages over
    Username     string // the only username createToken accepts
    Password     string // the only password createToken accepts
    AccessToken  string // the access token createToken hands out

    // RepeatBoundary pages the inventory the way a server with no stable
    // ordering does: every page after the first also starts with the last
    // element of the page before it.
    RepeatBoundary bool
}

type Request struct {
    Index       int         // position in the log
    OperationID string      // the contract operation the request matched, "" when it matched none
    Method      string
    Path        string
    RawQuery    string
    Header      http.Header
    Body        []byte
    Status      int         // the status the server answered with
}

type Server struct{ /* ... */ }

func New(cfg Config) (*Server, error) // starts the server
func (s *Server) URL() string         // http://127.0.0.1:<port>
func (s *Server) Requests() []Request // the log, in arrival order
func (s *Server) Close()
```

* `New` binds an ephemeral port on the loopback interface, reads the contract and the fixture, and reports an error if either is missing or if any of `Config`'s string fields is empty.
* Routing comes from the contract: only the method-and-path pairs it names are served. Anything else is `404`, logged with an empty `OperationID`.
* Every request is logged, whatever the outcome. `Requests` returns a snapshot the caller cannot use to mutate the server's copy.
* Failures answer with the specification's `Error` schema.
* `createToken`: a media type other than the contract's is `400`, though a `charset` parameter on the contract's own media type is still that media type; a body carrying a field outside the contract's property list for that body is `400`; a username or password other than `Config`'s is `400`. Otherwise the contract's success status for that operation, carrying a `TokenPair` whose access token is `Config.AccessToken`.
* `getHosts`, in this order:
  1. A missing, malformed or unrecognised `Bearer` token is `401`.
  2. A query parameter the contract does not list for this operation is `400` — this is what keeps the server pinned to the 9.0 revision. A repeated parameter is `400`; a parameter present with an empty value is `400`; a paging parameter that is not a non-negative integer is `400`.
  3. Otherwise filter the fixture, keeping fixture order, and answer with the requested page as a `PageOfHost`.
* Filtering matches exactly: `fqdn` and `status` against the host's own fields, `storageType` against `compatibleStorageType`, `datastoreName` against `bundleRepoDatastore`, and `domainId`, `clusterId` and `networkpoolId` against the id of the host's `domain`, `cluster` and `networkpool` — a host that has none of those never matches one.
* Paging: an absent or zero page size means a single page holding everything. Otherwise the page holds the window the page number and size select out of the matched hosts, plus, when `RepeatBoundary` is set and this is not the first page, the last element of the page before it at the front. The page metadata carries the page number as asked for, the number of elements on this page, the number of matched hosts, and the number of pages the size divides them into — `1` when there is no page size, and `0` when nothing matched.

## 4. `pkg/client` — the SDDC Manager client

```go
package client

type Config struct {
    BaseURL    string
    Username   string
    Password   string
    HTTPClient *http.Client // optional
}

type Filter struct { // every field optional
    FQDN          string
    Status        string
    DomainID      string
    ClusterID     string
    NetworkPoolID string
    StorageType   string
    DatastoreName string
    PageSize      int
}

type Host struct {
    ID                    string
    FQDN                  string
    ESXiVersion           string
    HardwareVendor        string
    HardwareModel         string
    Status                string
    CompatibleStorageType string
    DomainID              string
    ClusterID             string
    NetworkPoolID         string
    IPAddresses           []string
}

type Client struct{ /* ... */ }

func New(cfg Config) (*Client, error)
func (c *Client) ListHosts(ctx context.Context, f Filter) ([]Host, error)
```

* `New` rejects an empty `BaseURL`, `Username` or `Password`.
* `ListHosts` signs in once with `createToken`, then walks the inventory from the first page until it has seen every page the page metadata reports, keeping one copy of a host that arrives on more than one page.
* `DomainID`, `ClusterID` and `NetworkPoolID` come from the ids of the record's `domain`, `cluster` and `networkpool`, and stay empty when the record has none. `IPAddresses` are the record's addresses, in record order.
* The result is ascending by `FQDN`, compared byte by byte, and by `ID` when two hosts carry the same fqdn.
* A response that is not the operation's success status ends the sweep with an error that carries the status and what the `Error` body said.

## Request wire shape

* The paging page number is always sent. The page size is sent only when `Filter.PageSize` is greater than zero. Each of the seven filters is sent only when its field is non-empty. An unset optional parameter is left out of the query string entirely — never sent with an empty value.
* The `createToken` body is a JSON object carrying only the credential fields actually in use. The credential kinds the client is not using must not appear in the body at all, not even as empty strings.
* `Content-Type` is exactly `application/json`, and only on the request that carries a body.
* `createToken` carries no `Authorization` header and no query string. `getHosts` carries the access token as a `Bearer` token and no body.

## Tests

Write table-driven tests in `pkg/client` and `pkg/mock` covering, at least, the query strings the client builds, the body it sends to `createToken`, a sweep across pages that repeat their boundary element, and the mock's routing, paging, filtering and rejection paths.

`./scripts/verify.sh` must pass. It checks the deliverables are present and the protected files untouched, then runs `go vet` and `go test -race` over the module with the module proxy off. Everything it exercises is local — the mock binds to 127.0.0.1 and no VMware endpoint is contacted.
